sections.title: This week's likely biggest movers
sections.markdown:
Last week moved the AI trade's question from "is the build still growing?" to "will it be allowed and funded?" Suppliers kept beating (AMD, Arista, Super Micro, Vistra), yet the Democratic sweep, 40 of 41 local ballot measures against data centers, calls for a national moratorium, Microsoft pulling back from some neocloud contracts and CoreWeave bond yields above 16% gave the chip index its worst day since March 2020 on Nov 5 (AMD −17.7%, MU −17.2%, NVDA −9.3%). This week tests both halves: Constellation (Mon) on power, CoreWeave (Tue after close) and Nebius (Thu before open) on funding, Applied Materials, Cisco and Cerebras (Thu after close) on equipment, networking and AI-chip demand, all around October CPI (Tue) with December hike odds near 70–80% after hot payrolls. Nvidia (Nov 17) and Huang's requested House briefing (Nov 18) sit just past the window, and Nvidia's board opened an independent probe on Sunday. Last week's numbers and the full calendar are in the weekly brief. Each row names the trigger in both directions.

sections.title: Macro backdrop: hike odds back up, yields under 5%, oil under $100
sections.markdown:
Hot October payrolls put a December 9 hike back near 70–80% odds, but money hid in Treasuries during the AI selloff, so the 10-year sits near 4.86% and WTI near $90. Rates still cap the debt-funded AI builders first.

**Nov 4–6 update (midterms and jobs):** Democrats won both chambers. The first read was gridlock (megacaps and small caps up Nov 4); the second, from Nov 5, was AI policy: 40 of 41 local ballot measures restricting data centers passed, Texas's governor-elect called for a pause on new AI data center construction, and Democrats called for a national moratorium. Payrolls rose 165K against \~59–65K expected, unemployment fell to 4.1%, and futures put a December hike at roughly 70–80%. Figures are in Trade Desk's Nov 6 briefs. ([FXEmpire](https://www.fxempire.com/forecasts/article/the-week-ahead-cpi-and-tech-earnings-test-a-fragile-stock-market-1643118), [StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/ai-data-center-stocks-fall-texas-vote-november-4-2026), [KuCoin/news (Texas)](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/coreweave-stock-expected-to-swing-20-7-as-earnings-loom-amid-texas-and-debt-concerns))

**Week of Nov 9:** October CPI Tuesday at 8:30 a.m. (consensus 0.3% m/m, core 0.2%) is the last CPI before Dec 9 and will carry no year-over-year rate, because October 2025 was not collected during the shutdown, so the monthly core number is the whole signal. PPI follows Friday (0.4%, core 0.3%). About 15 Fed appearances run Monday to Friday, including Bowman and Barkin (Mon), Waller and Logan (Tue), Hammack, Williams and Daly (Thu). For this report the channel is funding cost for CoreWeave, Nebius and Oracle, and CoreWeave reports the evening of CPI day. Times and forecasts are in the weekly brief. ([FinancialJuice](https://features.financialjuice.com/2026/11/06/week-ahead-economic-indicators-9th-13th-november-us/), [FXEmpire](https://www.fxempire.com/forecasts/article/the-week-ahead-cpi-and-tech-earnings-test-a-fragile-stock-market-1643118))

**Oct 29 update:** Hot GDP and sticky PCE (figures in the morning brief) leave futures at \~84% odds of a December 9 hike, so long-duration AI names stay the market's funding source until that meeting. ([Barchart via Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stocks-trade-lower-alphabet-disappoints-150533033.html), [StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/stock-market-today-live-october-29-2026), [Fool](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/10/29/stock-market-today-oct-29-marvell-falls-on-lumentum-acquisition-talks/))

- Fed: held at 3.75%–4.00% in a 10–2 vote. Governor Lisa Cook (her first dissent) and Cleveland's Beth Hammack wanted a 25 bp hike. The statement said "the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine" the stance and called uncertainty elevated. Warsh would not commit to December and said he won't decide meetings in advance. Futures price roughly 83–85% odds of a December hike. ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/fed-votes-in-split-decision-to-hold-interest-rates-steady-despite-sticky-inflation-180108960.html), [KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/fed-chair-warsh-hesitates-on-december-rate-hike-amid-rising-treasury-yields), [TheStreet](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/the-fed-holds-oracle-jumps-chips-rise-for-fourth-session-but-alphabet-sinks-after-hours))
- Inflation: September CPI rose 3.7% (core 2.6%), up from 3.4% in August. ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/fed-votes-in-split-decision-to-hold-interest-rates-steady-despite-sticky-inflation-180108960.html))
- Rates: the 10-year rose about 5 bp to \~5.04% during the press conference while the 2-year fell to 4.70%. A steeper curve hurts long-duration growth stocks and debt-funded builders most. ([SRN News](https://srnnews.com/fomc-holds-rates-steady-markets-rise-modestly/))
- Stocks: the S&P 500 rose 0.3% to 7,743.98 and the chip index (SOX) 1.8%, its fourth straight gain. Utilities and real estate lagged on higher long yields. After hours, QQQ slipped \~0.5% on Alphabet. ([TheStreet](https://pro.thestreet.com/market-commentary/the-fed-holds-oracle-jumps-chips-rise-for-fourth-session-but-alphabet-sinks-after-hours), [RiskReversal](https://riskreversal.substack.com/p/fed-holds-msft-higher-googl-lower))
- Oil: Brent near $111 and WTI near $101. Iran's reply to Qatar's new draft deal is expected by week's end. ([investingLive](https://investinglive.com/news/investinglive-european-fx-news-wrap-28-oct/))
- AI financing: Alphabet's free cash flow was negative for a second straight quarter (−$9.1B). It raised $12.4B from share sales and $28.7B in debt during the quarter. ([Cautious Optimism](https://www.cautiousoptimism.news/msft-alpha-earnings), [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/10/28/alphabet-google-stock-drops-cloud-revenue-doubles-free-cash-flow-negative))
- Oct 30 oil-to-rates link: Brent up \~2.5% toward $117 adds to inflation pressure with September core PCE at 3.1%, which supports the \~83% December hike odds. That keeps pressure on long-duration AI names (CRWV, NBIS, ORCL) until Iran resolves. sections.title: Options timing: are earnings options cheap or expensive?
sections.markdown:
Last week's scorecard: after-hours beats did not hold. AMD, Arista and Super Micro all closed Nov 4 well inside their implied moves, and the Nov 5 selloff (SPY −4.4%) then swamped company news. Moves beyond implied came only from guide surprises: Datadog down on an in-line Q4, Cloudflare up premarket on a raise. Rich options (Coherent, ±16.0%) lost the most. This week CoreWeave's ±20.7–21.2% is the biggest priced move, and Applied Materials' ±10.4% is rich against its ±6.5% average. Buying calls or puts into a report only pays if the stock moves more than options already price in. Implied moves below are as of the date in each row and will shift.

**What this means for timing:**

1. When a report changes the guidance or funding story, history understates the move: Datadog this week, Alphabet and Intel before. History is a base rate, not a forecast.
2. After hours is not the close. Arista's +15% after hours became about +5% at the close and AMD's +7% about +1%. Averages above use closing moves where known; premarket figures are labeled.
3. Rich options (AMAT, CEG, CRWV against its average): buying calls or puts outright needs an outsized surprise; debit spreads cut the cost.
4. In a macro- or policy-driven tape, sector moves beat company news: Nov 5 moved AMD and MU more than any earnings report did.
5. Read-through names (MU, SKHY, VRT, GEV, ANET, ORCL) have no earnings premium of their own, so CoreWeave, Applied Materials and Cisco reprice them; Nvidia (Nov 17) is the group's next premium event.
6. Expiries: the first weekly after Tuesday's and Thursday's reports is Nov 13, the same morning as PPI. The Nov 20 expiry spans Nvidia's report and Huang's Nov 18 briefing.

Past moves don't predict the next one. Amazon confirmed the pattern: the market pays for cloud growth but sells negative free cash flow. AWS grew 39%, its fastest in nearly five years, yet the stock fell \~7% after hours because trailing free cash flow hit −$42.4B and 2027 capex goes higher still. Alphabet closed down 12.6% on the same worry.

sections.markdown:
Amazon is the new demand signal: Q3 capex of $77.3B, 2027 "meaningfully more," and Trainium commitments up more than 20x. Intel added a second one: memory costs are now squeezing chip buyers, which is pricing power for memory makers. Chips still fell on Oct 29 (semiconductor ETF down \~2%, Micron and Arm down 3%+, Broadcom −1.9%, Nvidia −0.8%) as Alphabet's drop and weak Korean memory results weighed. ([Barchart via Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stocks-trade-lower-alphabet-disappoints-150533033.html), [Fool](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/10/29/stock-market-today-oct-29-marvell-falls-on-lumentum-acquisition-talks/))

**Nov 3 update (AMD):** the memory-cost scare met its first big AI-chip answer. AMD beat its $12.7B–$13.3B guide (data center $8.5B, +97%) and guided Q4 to about $17B, with data center up \~50% sequentially and data center AI revenue passing server CPUs for the first time. Management said demand is above supply, that it is securing wafers, substrates, packaging and memory, and that customers are sharing component cost increases. The hit lands on PCs instead: client and gaming fall more than 20% next quarter and AMD plans for PC units down double digits in 2027. For the chain this splits cleanly: memory (MU, SKHY), foundry (TSM) and Helios server builders (SMCI, DELL, HPE) gain; PC-heavy names and Qualcomm carry the cost. ([AMD release](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/AMD/amd-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-7j6jzo29buqw.html), [TradingKey (call)](https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262270388-), [Phil Stock World](https://www.philstockworld.com/2026/11/03/after-hours-earnings-recap-amd-amgn-anet-alab-and-tost/))

**Nov 2 update:** Apple turned Intel's memory warning into a pattern. It said memory pricing is "unprecedented", that most of its December-quarter margin drop comes from memory, and that costs keep rising beyond December; it is offsetting with price increases and cheaper inventory that will run out. That is the clearest pricing-power signal yet for Micron and SK Hynix, and a cost warning for every device and server maker. The market sold chips anyway: the semiconductor ETF fell 3.8%, AMD 7.5%, Micron 5.8% and Intel 8.8%. ([9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/02/apple-says-memory-costs-and-siri-ai-will-weigh-on-holiday-quarter-profit-margins/), [Wall Street Republic](https://thewallstreetrepublic.substack.com/p/marvell-sinks-1272-on-a-115bn-lumentum))
